evidence.quote: The microstructure of the unalloyed MoSi 2 contained 91 vol% SiO 2 parti- cles, as estimated from a point counting method. Pre- sence of SiO 2 is more obvious from the polarized light optical micrograph of Fig. 3 [higher magniﬁcation of Fig. 2(a)].

The SiO 2 particles were replaced by Al 2O3 pre- cipitates in the MoSi 2–2.8, 5.5 and 9 at% Al alloys as shown in Fig. 2(b)–(d). The volume percentage of Al 2O3 particles in the MoSi 2–2.8, 5.5 and 9 at% Al alloys was estimated to be varying between 7 and 8, using a point counting method.

The volume percentage of Al 2O3 particles in the MoSi 2–2.8, 5.5 and 9 at% Al alloys was estimated to be varying between 7 and 8, using a point counting method.

The SiO 2 particles were replaced by Al 2O3 pre- cipitates in the MoSi 2–2.8, 5.5 and 9 at% Al alloys as shown in Fig. 2(b)–(d). The volume percentage of Al 2O3 particles in the MoSi 2–2.8, 5.5 and 9 at% Al alloys was estimated to be varying between 7 and 8, using a point counting method.

The microstructure of MoSi 2–9 at% Al alloy contained three phases, namely MoSi 2–3.1 at% Al alloy, Mo(Si,Al)2 phase and Al 2O3, as shown in the back- scattered electron image, and X-ray maps of Al, Si and O, respectively in Fig. 7(a)–(d). The Al enriched region in the matrix [Fig. 7(b)] corresponds to the Mo(Si,Al) 2 phase, which contained 8.7 at% Al.

The indentation crack paths in MoSi 2 were found to be predominantly transgranular (Fig. 18), similar to what has been observed in the fractographs and also reported by Wade and Petrovic [41]. However, the indentation fracture process was mainly intergranular in the MoSi 2–9 at% Al alloys (Fig. 19(a) and (b)).
